newsitem.title: USA: Primestar to expand TV service to 160 channels.
newsitem.headline: Primestar to expand TV service to 160 channels.

text.p: Primestar, a direct broadcast satellite television company, said Thursday it planned to expand its service to 160 channels from 95 beginning in April.

Chairman Jim Gray said the company expects to have signed up between 2.3 million and 2.4 million subscribers by the end of the year, which would edge Primestar over "our break even point." The company now has about 1.7 million subscribers.
Primestar is owned by a host of cable television operators.

The company's news conference Thursday to announce its expanded service comes at a time when the direct broadcast satellite industry is seeing increased competition, which could intensify in the next couple of years.

Earlier in the week, News Corp. Ltd., which owns the Fox television network, and EchoStar Communications Corp. said they planned to form an alliance to offer direct-broadcast satellite sevice with as many as 500 channels of digital TV, Internet services and local broadcast TV signals.
Primestar's expanded service would offer only a touch of local TV: local weather. Gray said its customers are likely to continue to receive their local television through a basic cable service.
Gray said he believed 1997 was a pivotal year for the industry. In contrast, the News Corp./EchoStar venture will not begin offering their service until early 1998.
"The key is to get the customer now," he said.

Suggested monthly retail prices for the service range from $32.99 to $59.99. A new remote was designed for the service, allowing viewers to hit colour-coded buttons to switch to a certain category of channels, such as music or sports.

Current subscribers will not have to get the new remote to avail themselves of the category-styled grouping of channels, Primestar said. Rather than hitting a different coloured button on a remote, they will need to type in a two-digit code.
Gray said it was unclear what kind of competition the News Corp./EchoStar venture would pose.
"None of us are going to know for some time," he said. "I think initially it doesn't do anything."

Combined, Primestar and DirecTV, which is owned by General Motors Corp.'s Hughes Electronics and AT&T Corp., have the largest block of the direct-broadcast satellite industry's 4.5 million subscribers. In contrast, there are about 64 million cable television subscribers in the United States.
Primestar is a partnership of a variety of subsidiaries, including those of Tele-Communications Inc., Time Warner Inc., Comcast Corp., and Cox Communications Inc.
